qid.description: <agent>-<YYYYMMDD>-<NNN>, shared by every artifact of one question (4.5.5)

thread.description: solo-<qid> when no bridge round is involved (5.2)

grade.description: Evidence grade (5.3). E6 may not appear in any card; the validator rejects it.

source.description: Where the number came from. The grade is derived from this prefix, never self-reported (check 21). operator_read is a value the operator read off the instrument; operator_recall is one they stated from memory, and the two do not deserve the same grade.

precision.description: order_of_magnitude means at most one significant figure is claimed (5.8, P15)

number.description: A value only means something with its unit, its source and its grade (P2).

formula.description: required when source is computed:. Arithmetic over other number names in this card.

inputs.description: required when source is computed:. Names this formula reads.

derived.description: true marks a dimensionless group (5.7). Uses a computed: source; not a separate source kind.

symbol.description: symbol of a dimensionless group, e.g. k_star

origin.description: for synthesis cards: <file>#<name> the value was carried from (check 12)

assumption.description: Every assumed: number must be explained here (check 4).

falsifier.description: what observation would retire this assumption

gap_ref.description: gap_id in kb_gaps: the librarian was asked and could not supply it (check 39). Required when the card reached the librarian at all; degraded says when it did not.

authorised_by.description: <person>_<yyyymmdd>, when a person directed that a value be carried past the range its source covers -- a curve's endpoint used for a wavelength beyond it, a spec read at one condition applied at another. It does NOT change the grade: being told to use a value is not evidence for it, and the moment an authorisation could lift E5 to E3 the grade scale becomes a permission scale and stops measuring anything. What it buys is the E5/E6 boundary. Once an extrapolation is written down as a number it looks identical whether a person directed it or a model invented it, and E5 may enter a card while E6 may enter nothing; without this field an auditor cannot tell them apart. A model may never fill it -- that would be a laundering path from E6 into a card. It belongs on the assumption and never on a KB entry: the entry says what is true at the condition its source covers, and who stretched it is a property of the plan that stretched it.

kb_ref.description: What the librarian returned, and the grade it returned it with (4.3.1).

kb_gap.description: What the librarian was asked for and could not supply (4.3.1). kb_refs records what came back; without this, what did not come back is recorded nowhere and the discovery of a gap dies with the server.

gap_id.description: what an assumption's gap_ref points at

kind.description: four kinds because the next action differs for each: search / find other conditions / ask a person / do not enter it (4.3.1)

searched.description: where it was looked for. A gap with nothing here is not a gap: not-looked-for and not-there are different claims.

nearest.description: entries that came close, so that 'nothing like it exists' and 'it exists at another temperature' stay distinguishable

overlap.description: How the near-miss entry stood against the query. `no_overlap` was called `unconstrained` until 2026-09-18, when that word was needed for a field meaning something else in the same response object (4.3.1 rule 3). **`unconstrained` is accepted only while the rename crosses seats and will be removed.** It cannot be dropped in the same commit that adds `no_overlap`: a card already on disk carries the old value, that card belongs to another seat, and until this enum accepts the new value that seat cannot write it -- so removing first deadlocks. Expand, migrate, contract. Holder as of 2026-09-18: microscope_agent/questions/mic-20260918-001/goal.json.

asked_by.description: the caller_id the fan-out executor issued (4.3.1)

criterion.description: Machine-readable stop/success criterion, declared before execution (5.4). A stop criterion also declares what being met means (on_met); a success criterion does not need to, because a success criterion being met is what success is.

number.description: name of the threshold in numbers[]

window.description: optional: over what interval the metric is evaluated

on_met.description: What it means for this criterion to be met. Without it `met: true` is not comparable between cards: result.json records sc_drift as met with outcome DONE, where met says the guard held, while a simulation's step_displacement_diverged is met exactly when the run broke. Same field, opposite meaning, and outcome is derived from it. continue: the condition still holds and the run proceeds; the stop is the violation. complete: the run has reached its planned end. fault: something broke and the run stops short of that end.

interval.description: An allowed range on one parameter. min or max may be absent (one-sided).

basis.description: names in numbers[] this bound rests on

condition_bound.description: One quantity's interval in canonical physical units (D7). min or max may be absent (one-sided), but not both.

condition_range.description: A map from quantity name to interval (4.3.1). Both sides of a condition query use this shape -- a query's condition_range and an entry's validity -- because one has to be compared against the other, and prose cannot be compared. That is why validity_conditions stays separate and human.

kb_gaps.description: the other side of kb_refs: asked for and not supplied. Not empty is normal (4.3). Every assumed: number points at one of these unless degraded says the librarian was never reached (check 39).

contrast.description: What a sample provides and a configuration requires. One list, two readers: a goal's sample_contrast and a capability's requires_contrast. Declared once because two parsers of one vocabulary drift, and the one that drifts says something false without erroring (0.4-6).
